description: Substitute Button/TextBox/CheckBox with Win11Button/Win11TextBox/Win11CheckBox in all 5 Designer.cs files, then build, commit, and push.
steps: Read each Designer.cs file fully before editing. The substitution rules are: (1) declaration lines 'private System.Windows.Forms.Button fieldName;' become 'private BulkCrapUninstaller.Controls.Win11Button fieldName;', (2) instantiation lines 'fieldName = new System.Windows.Forms.Button();' become 'fieldName = new BulkCrapUninstaller.Controls.Win11Button();', (3) same pattern for TextBox->Win11TextBox and CheckBox->Win11CheckBox, (4) for files that use short names (e.g. 'new Button()' and 'private Button fieldName'), substitute with 'new Win11Button()' and 'private Win11Button fieldName', and add 'using BulkCrapUninstaller.Controls;' at the top if not already present.
Apply substitutions to source/BulkCrapUninstaller/Forms/Windows/MainWindow.Designer.cs: buttonAdvFiltering (Button->Win11Button). Check for TextBox and CheckBox instances too.

Apply substitutions to source/BulkCrapUninstaller/Forms/Windows/SettingsWindow.Designer.cs: textBoxPreUninstall, textBoxPostUninstall (TextBox->Win11TextBox); checkBoxColorblind, checkBoxDpiaware, checkBoxAutoLoad, checkBoxRatings, checkBoxUpdateSearch, checkBoxSendStats, checkBoxShowAllBadJunk, checkBoxLoud, checkBoxNeverFeedback (CheckBox->Win11CheckBox); button2 (Button->Win11Button).

Apply substitutions to source/BulkCrapUninstaller/Forms/Windows/JunkRemoveWindow.Designer.cs: buttonCancel, buttonAccept, buttonExport (Button->Win11Button); checkBoxHideLowConfidence (CheckBox->Win11CheckBox).

Apply substitutions to source/BulkCrapUninstaller/Forms/Wizards/BeginUninstallTaskWizard.Designer.cs: buttonExit, buttonPrev, buttonNext, button2 — all 'new System.Windows.Forms.Button()' become 'new BulkCrapUninstaller.Controls.Win11Button()'. Also fix field declarations in the partial class (search for 'System.Windows.Forms.Button' field declarations and replace with 'BulkCrapUninstaller.Controls.Win11Button').
Run dotnet build and fix any compilation errors (e.g. if a field type was missed in the declaration section of a Designer.cs, or if a using directive is missing).

Once build passes with zero errors, run: git -C <workspace> add source/BulkCrapUninstaller/Theming/ source/BulkCrapUninstaller/Controls/Win11Button.cs source/BulkCrapUninstaller/Controls/Win11TextBox.cs source/BulkCrapUninstaller/Controls/Win11CheckBox.cs source/BulkCrapUninstaller/Forms/Windows/MainWindow.cs source/BulkCrapUninstaller/Forms/Windows/MainWindow.Designer.cs source/BulkCrapUninstaller/Forms/Windows/SettingsWindow.Designer.cs source/BulkCrapUninstaller/Forms/Windows/UninstallProgressWindow.Designer.cs source/BulkCrapUninstaller/Forms/Windows/JunkRemoveWindow.Designer.cs source/BulkCrapUninstaller/Forms/Wizards/BeginUninstallTaskWizard.Designer.cs
Commit: git commit -m 'feat(ui): Phase 1 – Win11 theme tokens, DWM Mica/dark-title-bar, Win11Button/TextBox/CheckBox controls'
acceptance_criteria: All 5 Designer.cs files have Win11Button/Win11TextBox/Win11CheckBox in place of the standard types
dotnet build exits with zero errors
git log shows the commit on feature/win11-ui
findings: Build passed with 0 errors, 0 warnings. Pushed to origin/feature/win11-ui (new branch). BeginUninstallTaskWizard.Designer.cs already had 'using BulkCrapUninstaller.Controls;' from FEAT-003; used fully-qualified BulkCrapUninstaller.Controls.Win11Button per instructions. SettingsWindow.Designer.cs had textBoxProgramFolders (TextBox) not in scope for substitution per instructions - left unchanged.
